overview.body: This self-study resource examines Roman roads as a connected infrastructure system that supported the expansion, administration, communication, and integration of the Roman Empire. You will investigate how roads were built, why they mattered, and how historians use evidence to interpret their significance.

learning_purpose.body: The resource enables you to explore Roman roads through historical explanation, analysis, evaluation, and synthesis. The activities develop an evidence-based understanding of the relationships between engineering, imperial governance, trade, communication, cultural exchange, and historical interpretation.

knowledge_summary.body: Roman roads formed a large-scale infrastructure network.

activities.title: Origins and Expansion of the Roman Road Network
activities.learner_task:
1. Study the explanatory text and worked example.
2. Examine the sample output and identify how evidence is linked to interpretation.
3. Create a brief concept map showing the links between imperial expansion, communication, administration, and road building.
4. Complete the verification checklist and revise your concept map if needed.
activities.expected_output: Produce a concise concept map and accompanying explanation that accurately connects Roman expansion to the development of the road network. Strong responses identify multiple functions of roads and explain how infrastructure supported imperial cohesion rather than merely listing facts.
activities.activity_preamble: Begin by building a foundation for the rest of the session.

learning_outcomes.statement: Describe the origins and expansion of the Roman road network.
